answer: Put a price on sloth in judgment itself: every graded ballot must be countersigned with a small stake. A juror who rubber-stamps like a parrot, merely echoing the crowd, invites an appeal window where a randomly drafted jury forges a second verdict from the raw text. Uphold the lazy ballot and the appellant; overturn it and the slothful slot forfeits its stake to the challenger. Good reviews are laid like marble, one careful cut at a time, and lost in a single reckless afternoon.
